steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the vue module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to Vue and the ref function for creating reactive references.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref, which are essential for this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create a parent component with template
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ParentComponent that returns a template section with a single root <div> element.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component can be defined as a function that returns an object with a template property. The template should contain a single root element.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create a Vue component named ParentComponent
steps.expectedOutcome: A ParentComponent function is defined that returns an object with a template property containing a <div> as the root element.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is defined as a function that returns an object with a template property containing a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ParentComponent with a template structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the component, but make sure it returns an object with a template property containing a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named ParentComponent that returns an object with a template property containing a <div> element.

steps.title: Initialize a ref in parent component
steps.instruction: Inside the ParentComponent's setup function, initialize a reactive reference using the ref() function you imported. Name this reference 'inputRef'.
steps.hint: Use the ref() function from Vue to create a reactive reference that will hold a DOM element reference.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive reference
const myRef = ref(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent will have a reactive reference named 'inputRef' initialized in its setup function.
successCriteria: A ref named 'inputRef' is created using the ref() function inside the ParentComponent's setup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized a reactive reference that will be used to access a DOM element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ref() function from Vue and naming the reference 'inputRef'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref wasn't properly initialized. Check that you're using the ref() function from Vue inside the setup function.

steps.title: Create a child component with template
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ChildComponent with a template section that contains a single <input> element.
steps.hint: Define a new component object with a name property and a template property. The template should contain an <input> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent is defined with a template containing an <input> element, ready to be used by the parent component.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined with name: 'ChildComponent' and template: '<input />'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the child component with an input element. This component will later be used with forwardRef to expose its DOM node.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named 'ChildComponent' and has a template with an <input> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component isn't properly defined. Create a Vue component named ChildComponent with a template containing an <input> element.

steps.title: Define props in child component to accept ref
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent, define props to accept a forwarded ref from the parent. Add a props option with a property named 'forwardedRef'.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define props in the component options. Add a 'props' property with an array or object that includes 'forwardedRef'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent now has a props definition that includes 'forwardedRef', allowing it to receive a ref from the parent component.
successCriteria: The ChildComponent has a 'props' property defined with 'forwardedRef' included.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined props in the ChildComponent to accept a forwarded ref. This prepares the component to receive a ref from its parent.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a 'props' property to the ChildComponent with 'forwardedRef' included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent still needs a props definition. Add a 'props' property with 'forwardedRef' to accept the forwarded ref.

steps.title: Add input element in child template
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent, add a template section with an input element that will be exposed to the parent via ref.
steps.hint: Add a template section with an input element. This will be the DOM element that the parent component can access.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent now has a template section containing an input element that can be targeted by a ref.
successCriteria: ChildComponent has a template property with an input element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an input element to the child component's template. This is the DOM node that will be exposed to the parent.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a template property with an input element inside the ChildComponent object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent should have a template property containing an input element. Check that you've added the template correctly.

steps.title: Bind ref to input element using v-bind
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent template, bind the forwarded ref prop to the input element's ref attribute using v-bind.
steps.hint: Use v-bind (or the shorthand :) to connect the ref prop to the input's ref attribute.
steps.analogousExample:
// Binding a prop to an element attribute
<template>
  <input :ref="forwardedRef" />
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element in ChildComponent will have its ref attribute bound to the forwardedRef prop, allowing the parent to access the input's DOM node.
successCriteria: The ChildComponent template includes an input element with :ref="forwardedRef" binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully bound the forwarded ref to the input element. This allows the parent component to directly access the input's DOM node.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using v-bind (or :) to bind the forwardedRef prop to the input's ref attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element needs to have its ref attribute bound to the forwardedRef prop using v-bind syntax.

steps.title: Add child component to parent template with ref binding
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent's template, add the ChildComponent and bind the parent's ref to the forwardedRef prop.
steps.hint: Use the child component's tag name and bind the ref using v-bind or the colon shorthand.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a child component with prop binding
<template>
  <ChildComponent :forwardedRef="myRef" />
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component's template includes the child component with the ref properly passed as a prop.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is added to ParentComponent's template
Parent's ref is bound to forwardedRef prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the child component and passed the parent's ref as a prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the child component, but make sure to bind the parent's ref to the forwardedRef prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component is not properly added or the ref binding is missing.

steps.title: Add button to parent template to focus input
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent's template, add a button element with the text 'Focus Input' that will trigger a function to focus the child's input element.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the template section of ParentComponent. You'll need to create a click handler function in the next step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to a template template: `
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent template now contains a button element that will be used to trigger focus on the child's input.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Focus Input' is added to the ParentComponent template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the button that will control the focus action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Focus Input'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrectly placed in the ParentComponent template.

steps.title: Implement button click handler to focus input
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent's setup function, create a click handler function named handleFocus that accesses the input element via the inputRef and calls its focus() method.
steps.hint: Inside the setup function, define a function that uses the ref's value property to get the DOM element and call focus() on it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have a working click handler that focuses the input element in the child component when clicked.
successCriteria: A handleFocus function is defined in ParentComponent's setup that accesses inputRef.value and calls focus().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the click handler that accesses the DOM element through the forwarded ref and focuses it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleFocus function accesses the ref's value property and calls focus() on it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click handler isn't implemented correctly. Remember to define handleFocus in the setup function and use inputRef.value.focus().
